title: 1979 AHSME Problem 5
statement: Find the sum of the digits of the largest even three digit number (in base ten representation) which is not changed when its units and hundreds digits are interchanged.

solutions.text:
The equal hundreds and units digit must be even. The largest possible nonzero such digit is \(8,\) and the tens digit can be \(9.\) Thus the largest number is \(898,\) whose digit sum is \(8+9+8=25.\)

Therefore, the correct answer is D.
hints: The hundreds and units digits must be equal
Maximize the equal outer digits subject to the number being even, then maximize the tens digit
